descriptionChirho: The noun kur (כּוּר) meaning 'furnace, smelting furnace' — a vessel or installation used for refining metals, frequently used both literally and as a metaphor for affliction and testing. Appears in Deut 4:20, 1 Kgs 8:51, Jer 11:4 (Egypt as an iron furnace), Prov 17:3, 27:21 (crucible for refining silver/gold), Isa 48:10 (furnace of affliction), and Ezek 22:18,20,22 (Jerusalem as a smelting furnace). English renders as furnace; Spanish horno; Hindi भट्ठी (bhatthi) 'kiln/furnace'; Arabic كُور (kur) 'furnace/bellows'; Korean 용광로 (yonggwangro) 'smelting furnace' / 풀무 (pulmu) 'bellows'; Swahili tanuru 'furnace.' Both clusters express the same noun — the second simply has prepositional prefixes (in/from the furnace of), not a different meaning.
